units.text: # Installation

This guide uses ⟦0⟧ (via miniforge) to manage environments (recommended). If you prefer another environment manager (e.g. ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧), ensure you have Python >=3.12 and support PyTorch >= 2.10, then skip ahead to [Environment Setup](⟦3⟧).

### Install ⟦0⟧ (for video decoding)
LeRobot uses [TorchCodec](⟦0⟧) for video decoding by default, which requires ⟦1⟧.

> [!NOTE]
> **Platform support:** TorchCodec is **not available** on macOS Intel (x86_64), Linux ARM (aarch64, arm64, armv7l), or Windows with PyTorch < 2.8. On these platforms, LeRobot automatically falls back to ⟦0⟧ — so you do not need to install ⟦1⟧ and can skip to Step 3.

> **Jetson (aarch64 + CUDA):** the ⟦0⟧ fallback above means no GPU-accelerated video decode by default. [⟦1⟧](⟦2⟧) builds ⟦3⟧/⟦4⟧ from source with CUDA support for JetPack 6.2 — community-maintained, see [⟦5⟧](⟦6⟧) for the prebuilt image and issue [#819](⟦7⟧) for background.
If your platform supports TorchCodec, install ⟦0⟧ using one of the methods below:

Starting with **PyTorch >= 2.10** (TorchCodec ≥ 0.10), TorchCodec can dynamically link to a system-wide ⟦0⟧ installation. This is useful when using ⟦1⟧ or other non-⟦2⟧ environment managers:

> [!IMPORTANT]
> System-wide ⟦0⟧ is **only supported with PyTorch >= 2.10** (TorchCodec ≥ 0.10). For older PyTorch versions, you **must** use ⟦1⟧ instead.
## Step 3: Install LeRobot 🤗

The base ⟦0⟧ install is intentionally **lightweight** — it includes only core ML dependencies (PyTorch, torchvision, numpy, opencv, einops, draccus, huggingface-hub, gymnasium, safetensors). Heavier dependencies are gated behind optional extras so you only install what you need.

### Installation from PyPI

**Core Library:**
Install the base package with:
_This installs only the core ML dependencies. You will need to add extras for most workflows._

**Feature Extras:**
LeRobot provides **feature-scoped extras** that map to common workflows. If you are using ⟦0⟧, replace ⟦1⟧ with ⟦2⟧ in the commands below.
| Extra      | What it adds                                | Typical use case                    |
| ⟦0⟧  | ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ | Loading & creating datasets         |
| ⟦0⟧ | ⟦1⟧ + ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧           | Training policies                   |
| ⟦0⟧ | ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧            | Connecting to real robots           |
| ⟦0⟧      | ⟦1⟧                                 | Visualization during recording/eval |
**Composite Extras** combine feature extras for common CLI scripts:
| Extra          | Includes                       | Typical use case                                        |
| ⟦0⟧   | ⟦1⟧                           | ⟦2⟧ (add policy + env extras as needed)      |
**Policy, environment, and hardware extras** are still available for specific dependencies:
_Multiple extras can be combined (e.g., ⟦0⟧). For a full list of available extras, refer to ⟦1⟧._
### PyTorch CUDA variant (Linux only)
On Linux, the install path determines which CUDA wheel you get. macOS and Windows installs use the PyPI default (MPS / CPU / CUDA-Windows wheel respectively) and can skip this section.
**Source install via ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧)**
⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are pinned by the project to the **CUDA 12.8** PyTorch index (⟦2⟧, driver floor **570.86**) — covers Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell GPUs. No action needed for typical NVIDIA setups.
To override for a different CUDA variant:
**Source install via ⟦0⟧/⟦1⟧, or ⟦2⟧ from PyPI**
PyPI default torch wheel is currently a cu130-bundled Linux wheel, driver floor **580.65**.
To pick a specific CUDA variant:

## Optional dependencies

LeRobot provides optional extras for specific functionalities. Multiple extras can be combined (e.g., ⟦0⟧). For all available extras, refer to ⟦1⟧. If you are using ⟦2⟧, replace ⟦3⟧ with ⟦4⟧ in the commands below.
### Simulations

Install environment packages: ⟦0⟧ ([gym-aloha](⟦1⟧)), or ⟦2⟧ ([gym-pusht](⟦3⟧)).
These automatically include the ⟦4⟧ extra.
### Motor Control
For Koch v1.1 install the Dynamixel SDK, for SO100/SO101/Moss install the Feetech SDK.
